html:
A Nigerian thriller released straight onto video cassette in two parts, in 1992 and 1993. Its success is usually taken as the birth of Nollywood, the film industry of Nigeria.

Written by Kenneth Nnebue and Okechukwu Ogunjiofor and made in the Igbo language, it tells of Andy, a struggling man in Lagos who joins a secret cult and sacrifices his wife for wealth, then is haunted by her ghost. Kenneth Okonkwo and Nnenna Nwabueze became stars through it.

The film was cheap to make and was sold on VHS tapes in markets for people to watch at home. Cinemas were few at the time, so home video suited buyers. Thousands of films a year followed the same way, shot fast on small budgets, telling stories of money, faith, family and the supernatural. Nollywood now makes more films than almost any other industry in the world and is watched across Africa and its diaspora. A sequel, Living in Bondage: Breaking Free, came out in 2019.
sum: A Nigerian thriller released straight onto video cassette in two parts, in 1992 and 1993. Its success is usually taken as the birth of Nollywood, the film industry of Nigeria.
